data.narrative:
Runpod, a Series C-stage chip and semiconductor company founded by Zhen Lu and Pardeep Singh, has raised $122.3M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 8 private and 3 public semiconductor firms, including peers such as Tenstorrent ($2.7B), Nearfield Instruments ($1.6B), DEEPX ($529M), and Positron AI ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $208M based on the $122M total raised proxy. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies produces a $1.3B midpoint valuation, with a range spanning $529M to $2.7B. Public-comp anchoring using semiconductor P/S multiples (median 20.4x across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) is not applicable absent disclosed revenue.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $177M (low) to $1.5B (high), with a median of $754M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around Runpod's revenue scale, growth trajectory, and competitive positioning relative to better-capitalized peers like Tenstorrent. Stage-progression and peer-median methods diverge significantly, with the former anchored to funding history and the latter to market comparables. Revenue disclosure or clearer narrative on customer concentration and margin profile would narrow this range materially.
